summary: A satirical local-news piece mocking a city council's City-Wide Recycling Mandates, unveiled September 6, 2023. It lampoons absurd rules such as the Bin Alignment Scheme, the Trash Taskforce, gimmicky 'Gadgets for Garbage', and an incinerator incentive. It ends by questioning whether the green initiative will succeed or just baffle citizens.
one_line: A satirical account of a city council's absurd City-Wide Recycling Mandates, from bin-angle rules to compost gadgets and an incinerator incentive.
key_facts: The City-Wide Recycling Mandates were unveiled at City Hall on September 6, 2023, on a Wednesday evening.
Mayor Marlene Muckraker wore a suit made of recycled plastic bottles and declared, "The time has come to correct our community's cavalier crap-creating customs!"
The council debated what belongs in the blue bins, such as greasy pizza boxes and plastic bottle caps, and drew lots to decide which item to consider next.
The Bin Alignment Scheme (B.A.S.) assigns households a geometric sequence dictating the positioning of their bins.
Councilwoman Prudence Prisel said blue bins would be placed at a 45-degree angle towards the North Star on every second Thursday following a full moon.
The Trash Taskforce is a group of pedantic policy enthusiasts with clipboards and binoculars that patrols neighborhoods checking bin alignment.
One Trash Taskforce officer warned a citizen that a milk jug facing eastward was an affront to the B.A.S. and threatened an official reprimand.
Citizens were promised 'Gadgets for Garbage', including the compost communicator presented by technologist-in-residence Harold Hack-a-lot.
The compost communicator reminds users of decomposing items through spoken-word riddles, such as one about a banana peel.
Councilman Ignatius Ignite proposed the Illustrious Incinerator Incentive, with the motto "Rise from the ashes, like the refuse phoenix you're fated to be!"
A proposal to turn discarded toasters and duvets into power for street lamps was called "ingeniously impractical" and filed under "perhaps...someday."
The piece concludes that it is unclear whether the recycling mandates will triumph or be tossed aside; citizens are left with color-coded calendars and thick bylaw binders.
